# Psalm 57 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. A psalm of David, regarding the time he fled from Saul and went into the cave. To the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.'

**2** Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy! I look to You for protection. I will hide beneath the shadow of Your wings until the danger passes by.

**3** I cry out to God Most High, to God who will fulfill His purpose for me.

**4** He will send help from heaven to rescue me, disgracing those who hound me. Pause and reflect. My God will send forth His unfailing love and faithfulness.

**5** I am surrounded by fierce lions who greedily devour human prey — whose teeth pierce like spears and arrows, and whose tongues cut like swords.

**6** Be exalted, O God, above the highest heavens! May Your glory shine over all the earth.

**7** My enemies have set a trap for me. I am weary from distress. They have dug a deep pit in my path, but they themselves have fallen into it! Pause and reflect.

**8** My heart is confident in You, O God; my heart is confident. No wonder I can sing Your praises!

**9** Wake up, my heart! Wake up, O lyre and harp! I will wake the dawn with my song.

**10** I will thank You, Lord, among all the people. I will sing Your praises among the nations.

**11** For Your unfailing love is as high as the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **57:7-8**: The dramatic pivot: from lions and traps (vv.4-7a) to steadfast confidence and dawn-waking music (vv.7b-9). The cave becomes a concert hall.

— PNEUMA
